name: Call of Duty 4: Modern Warfare

scale.why: 1 unit = 1 inch (the CoD modding wiki's study), 0.0254 m/u; the player box height isn't published, so not rescaled to 1.8 m

speed.source: https://wiki.zeroy.com/index.php/Call_of_Duty_:_A_Study_on_FPS (max forward run 190 u/s with an SMG, trench gun or sniper class)
speed.note: weapon-dependent: assault class 180, machine gunner 166; strafe 152, back 133

jump.note: CoD sets the jump by its height (jump_height), not a speed

friction.note: the dvar list's default; the Quake friction formula (CoD's movement is Quake III-derived)

jumpHeight.source: https://github.com/callofduty4x/CoD4x_Server/blob/master/src/bg_jump.cpp#L358 (jump_height 39.0, 'the maximum height of a player's jump')
jumpHeight.note: measured 39.5-42 u depending on frame rate (125 fps: 41); Quark: 1.22 m

extras: jump slowdown: landing cuts speed to x0.65 (x0.5 after a high fall) for a moment (bg_jump.cpp#L330-350, jump_slowdownEnable 1)
jump_stepSize 18: the step up allowed at the top of a jump arc
mantling, frame-rate dependent jump heights (the 125 / 250 / 333 fps tricks)
notes: CoD4's game code isn't public; the CoD4x server (a reverse-engineered rewrite) gives jump_height, a dvar list gives friction, a host's config gives gravity, and the run speeds are a modder's measurements. Modern Call of Duty (MW2019 / MWII / BO6) publishes no movement values; community testing (TrueGameData) gives sprint speeds (BO6 SMGs 6.6-6.7 m/s, pistols 6 m/s) but no base speed, gravity or jump, so those games aren't covered.

sources.title: CoD modding wiki: A Study on FPS (run speeds, jump heights)
WZ Stats (TrueGameData): BO6 close range stats
